sequence_description: I1 proof/consumer mismatch via token exchange: obtain a subject token for one identity, then attempt token exchange for a different audience/resource; broker must not treat the exchanged token as proof for a different semantic context without proper verification.
description: [LLM-Judge] Token introspection returned an entity_id (subject) even though the token was inactive after a failed token-exchange attempt, suggesting possible response/variable mix-up or introspection leakage.

sequence_description: Obtain a subject token via password login, perform token exchange once, revoke the original subject token, then attempt token exchange again using the revoked subject token; second exchange must be rejected if freshness/revocation is enforced.
description: [LLM-Judge] Session/token revocation step failed with invalid_client, so the replay-after-revocation invariant was not actually exercised; indicates a potential misbinding/misuse of the revocation endpoint or client authentication requirements.

sequence_description: Attempt to replay an OIDC authorization code after exchanging it once and revoking the resulting access token; the same code must not be usable twice (anti-replay). Uses two identities to ensure the second exchange is not accidentally tied to the first session.
description: [LLM-Judge] Authorization-code exchange failed with invalid_client, so the anti-replay invariant was not actually exercised; additionally, the captured 'alice' exchange identity maps to Bob's user_id, suggesting a test harness/session mix-up that could mask real replay behavior.

evidence.llm_judge_description: Authorization-code exchange failed with invalid_client, so the anti-replay invariant was not actually exercised; additionally, the captured 'alice' exchange identity maps to Bob's user_id, suggesting a test harness/session mix-up that could mask real replay behavior.

description: [LLM-Judge] Flow coherence test is invalid/inconclusive: the OIDC authorization start step failed (404), yet an SSO login succeeded via a different endpoint, so nonce-bypass/step-skipping cannot be established from this trace.

sequence_description: Cross-protocol identity merge: local password user (victim) vs OIDC enterprise SSO principal (attacker_sub) claiming the same VERIFIED email. Expectation: should NOT collapse distinct upstream principals into the same downstream subject unless explicitly intended; detect unintended account takeover via email-based linking.
description: [LLM-Judge] Enterprise OIDC SSO login was linked to an existing local-password account solely by matching a verified email, causing two security-distinct upstream principals to map to the same downstream subject (potential account takeover if the IdP is attacker-controlled or email verification is not strongly trusted).
